Class PythonFixedAttributes

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.context.python.PythonFixedAttributes
@Internal public final class PythonFixedAttributes extends Object
The attributes of the objects of a Python class that the statically compiled bodies of its stub read from Java fields: attributes fixed at construction, which __init__ assigns and nothing in the compilation writes afterwards (see StaticPlanner.fixed_attribute). One instance per stub class holds the epoch of those fields; each stub holds one PythonFixedAttributes.Slot per attribute.

A slot reads the attribute through the Python object the first time and keeps the converted value, for that Python object, until the epoch moves on: once a slot has read an attribute of an object (micronaut_runtime.__micronaut_fixed_member), the class's __setattr__ and __delattr__ report every change of that attribute, by name, of an object of the class, so a write the compilation does not see (a test's monkeypatch.setattr, code outside the compilation) makes the slots read the attribute again. A write of an attribute no slot holds (a counter the compilation mutates) reports nothing and keeps the slots' values. The epoch is one per stub class rather than one per attribute: the compilation never writes a fixed attribute, so a reported change is rare, and a single epoch keeps the read a field comparison. An object whose class serves its attributes itself (a __getattribute__, a __setattr__ of its own, a class attribute of the name) is read every time, as the stub reads any other attribute.

A stub primes its slots when it takes its Python object (prime(Value, String[], PythonFixedAttributes.Slot[], PolyglotValueConverter[], boolean[])): when it is created, wraps an object, or creates its object again, so a compiled body does not read an attribute through the Python object the first time it runs (a route kept on the event loop, see EventLoopSafety, then never waits for the context). Only an attribute the object has is primed; a slot of one it lacks (yet) reads it as before. A slot reads its attribute again after a reported change, on whichever thread runs the next body: by the planner's rules only code outside the compilation writes a fixed attribute. A cycle of objects holding each other in fixed attributes leaves the slots of the wrapper that closes the cycle to their first read.

    • prime

      public void prime(@Nullable org.graalvm.polyglot.Value self, String[] names, PythonFixedAttributes.Slot[] slots, PolyglotValueConverter<?>[] converters, boolean[] wrappers)
      Fills the slots of a stub for its Python object, in one call into Python, when the stub takes the object: each slot keeps the value of its attribute as its first read would, so the compiled bodies read none of them through the object. A slot of an attribute the object does not have (yet) is left empty, and a value that does not convert is left to the read, which fails as before. A wrapper the conversion creates primes its own slots; one of an object being primed on this thread does not, which ends a cycle of objects holding each other.
      Parameters:
      self - The Python object of the stub
      names - The attributes, one per slot
      slots - The slots of the stub
      converters - The conversion of each attribute to the Java type the bodies read
      wrappers - Whether each type is the generated class of a plain class of the compilation
